narrative:
The model estimates a 62% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

The strongest influence was that you have received other job opportunities while at your company. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with a higher likelihood of leaving, and in your case it strongly pushed the prediction toward departure.

Next, your total years of experience across all jobs worked against the prediction. With only 1-5 years of overall experience (compared to 50% of employees predicted to stay also being in this range), this factor pulled the outcome back toward staying. However, its stabilizing effect was not enough to overcome the other influences.

The third most important factor was your employment in the “other” sector. This category, which represents about 22% of employees predicted to stay, contributed noticeably toward the model expecting you to leave.

Taken together, the combination of active external opportunities and your sector outweighed the protective effect of your relatively short overall experience, tipping the balance to a 62% probability of leaving.

The organization should discuss with you whether those external offers can be matched internally or if additional support in your current role could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what those outside opportunities offer that your current position does not. Addressing these points could improve your chances in future promotion reviews.
